page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 959 GB SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals significant performance tradeoffs for the ecs.i2.xlarge. The Intel Xeon 8163 processor delivers single-core and multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25% of tested servers, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only operations falling into the bottom 10% and write operations in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%. These results indicate that while the instance provides a high storage-to-vCPU ratio, its computational and memory throughput capabilities are limited.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2.xlarge represents a resource-density tradeoff, offering a substantial 959 GB local SSD and 32.0 GB of RAM at a lower tier of processing performance. This makes it appropriate for workloads that require significant local storage capacity and moderate memory space but do not demand high CPU or memory throughput. Appropriate workloads include localized file caching, lightweight database hosting with low transaction volumes, basic data logging, and general-purpose tasks that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local SSD storage without intensive computational requirements.
